contentHtml:
Hyderabad: Suven Life Sciences Ltd. has randomized the first patient in its Phase 3 AWAKE clinical study evaluating Samelisant (SUVN-G3031) for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) in adults with narcolepsy.

The first patient was randomized at a clinical trial site in the United States, marking an important milestone in the development of the investigational drug, the clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company said.

Samelisant is a potent and selective histamine H3 receptor inverse agonist designed to enhance histaminergic neurotransmission and promote wakefulness. The drug is being developed for the treatment of excessive daytime sleepiness in patients with both Narcolepsy Type 1 (NT1) and Narcolepsy Type 2 (NT2).

While NT1 is characterized by orexin deficiency and cataplexy, NT2 is primarily characterized by excessive daytime sleepiness without cataplexy.

Suven's Phase 3 AWAKE Study Design

The global Phase 3 AWAKE study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicentre clinical trial being conducted across North America, including the United States and Canada, and Europe, including Italy, France, Germany and Spain.

The study plans to enroll approximately 240 adults diagnosed with NT1 or NT2. Participants will be randomized to receive either Samelisant or a placebo.

The trial comprises a four-week screening period, followed by a 12-week treatment period and a subsequent safety follow-up period.

Suven expects to complete enrolment of the last participant by December 2027, with topline results anticipated in the first half of 2028.

The primary objective is to evaluate the efficacy of Samelisant in improving excessive daytime sleepiness, measured using the Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS).

The study will also assess objective wakefulness through the Maintenance of Wakefulness Test (MWT), along with other clinically relevant measures of narcolepsy symptoms and patient outcomes. These include weekly cataplexy rates, attention, vigilance, cognitive performance and functional outcomes. The safety and tolerability of Samelisant will also be evaluated.

Samelisant Targets Unmet Needs in Narcolepsy Treatment

Despite the availability of several approved treatments for narcolepsy, some patients continue to experience residual symptoms or require individualized treatment approaches, according to the company.

Treatment selection can be influenced by factors such as side effects, tolerability, drug interactions, dosing requirements and controlled-substance considerations.

Samelisant works through histaminergic modulation by targeting H3 receptors, which play a role in regulating wakefulness. Suven said the drug's pharmacological profile and findings from its Phase 2 clinical study provide a scientific rationale for further evaluation in patients with narcolepsy.

The company is developing Samelisant as a potential treatment for both NT1 and NT2. Its mechanism of action and safety profile could potentially offer an additional treatment option for patients living with the disorder.

Management Commentary

Commenting on the milestone, Venkat Jasti, Chairman and Managing Director of Suven Life Sciences, said the randomization of the first patient in the Phase 3 AWAKE study marks an important step in the company's efforts to advance innovative therapies for central nervous system disorders.

He said narcolepsy continues to represent a significant unmet medical need despite the availability of existing treatment options. The company believes Samelisant's differentiated pharmacological profile and potential applicability across both major forms of narcolepsy could make it an important addition to the treatment landscape.

Ramakrishna Nirogi, President and Chief Scientific Officer of Suven Life Sciences, said Samelisant is being developed based on histaminergic modulation through H3 receptor inverse agonism.

He noted that histamine plays an important role in regulating wakefulness and that the encouraging Phase 2 findings provide a scientific rationale for advancing the drug into Phase 3 evaluation.

The AWAKE study is designed to comprehensively assess the efficacy and safety of Samelisant, particularly its potential to improve excessive daytime sleepiness in patients with NT1 and NT2, he added.

Suven Life Sciences' Clinical Pipeline

Suven Life Sciences is focused on discovering and developing innovative therapies for central nervous system disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, sleep disorders, major depressive disorder, Parkinson's disease, schizophrenia and pain disorders.

The company's clinical-stage pipeline includes Masupirdine (SUVN-502), which is being evaluated for agitation in patients with Alzheimer's disease dementia in a global Phase 3 study. Enrolment in the trial has been completed.

Other clinical candidates include Ropanicant (SUVN911) for major depressive disorder, Usmarapride (SUVN-D4010) and Tenaclidine (SUVN-I6107) for cognitive disorders, and Samelisant for excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy.

Samelisant has completed a Phase 2 study for excessive daytime sleepiness, while its pivotal Phase 3 AWAKE study is now underway. The company is also planning a Phase 2 study to evaluate the drug for cataplexy.
